description: bb plugins by Kalindu De Costa.

categories.description: Change what people see or do inside an open thread.
Change how threads are listed and organized in the sidebar.
Create and manage where threads run, locally or in the cloud.
Plan, track, route, schedule, or automate work.

plugins.description: Run your own prompt files from ~/.agents/commands in any bb thread. Type ! for a menu of them, or type /name as you would in pi: codex and Claude Code agents learn to run it, and pi expands it itself.
plugins.overview:
Use your own slash-command prompts from `~/.agents/commands` in any bb thread, whichever agent runs it.

## What you get

- Type `!` in a composer to open a Commands menu listing every `.md` file in `~/.agents/commands`, with its description and argument hint. The list is read fresh from disk as you type, so a new or edited file shows up straight away.
- Pick a command, type its arguments after it, and send. The plugin attaches the command's instructions to your message for the agent, and you see only the pill and your arguments in the thread.
- Type `/name arguments` as plain text and it works too. Codex and Claude Code agents are told which commands exist and to run `/name` from the folder. pi expands `/name` itself when `~/.pi/agent/prompts` links to `~/.agents/commands`, so the plugin adds nothing to pi threads in that case.

## The command files

Each command is one Markdown file in pi's prompt template format. The file name is the command name, `description` and `argument-hint` come from the frontmatter, and the body can use `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1` and `${@:2}` for the arguments:

```markdown
---
description: Review staged git changes
argument-hint: "[focus]"
---
Review the staged changes. Focus on ${1:-correctness}.
```

To keep pi on the same files, make its prompts folder a link: `ln -s ../../.agents/commands ~/.pi/agent/prompts`.

## Limits

- bb's `/` menu is fed by skills and the agent's own command folders, and plugins cannot add to it, so the menu uses `!`.
- A `!` command attaches its text when you send, before bb knows the message, so the placeholders are not filled in. The agent is told that the rest of your message is the arguments and how `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1` and `${@:N}` map onto it.
- Typed `/name` has been tested in pi and codex threads. The `!` menu does not depend on the agent, because bb attaches the command text itself.
- The menu reads the folder on the machine that runs the bb server. Typed `/name` commands are read by the agent on the thread's own machine.
- Only top-level `.md` files with names made of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` are listed, like pi.

plugins.description: Expands thinking blocks in threads automatically and keeps streaming thinking scrolled into view. Toggle it from the thread header or a thread's actions menu.
plugins.overview:
Watch an agent reason without clicking each thinking row open and scrolling inside it while the text streams.

## What you get

- The live **Thinking…** row at the bottom of a running thread opens by itself and stays scrolled to its newest line.
- Finished **Thought** rows open when they appear, including the ones inside an activity group once you open that group.
- Scroll up inside a thinking block to read earlier text and it stops following; scroll back to the bottom and it follows again.
- A block you collapse stays collapsed.
- A brain button in the thread header turns the plugin on or off, and so do the **Follow thinking** item in any thread's actions menu (the one phones use, since their header leaves the button out) and the command **Follow Thinking: Toggle auto-expand and auto-scroll of thinking** in the command palette. Turning it off collapses the blocks it opened and leaves the ones you opened.

## How it works

The plugin runs in the bb window and works on the timeline bb already draws. It needs no account, settings or server state. The on/off choice is saved on each device and shared by every bb window there.

## Limits

bb has no plugin interface for timeline rows, so the plugin recognises thinking blocks by the markup that bb 0.46 draws. If a bb update changes that markup, the plugin stops doing anything until it is updated; the timeline itself keeps working.

plugins.description: Open this bb from phones and laptops on your home network: pair a device once with a code or QR code, then use bb in its browser at <computer>.local, its LAN IP or your own name. No bb account or getbb.app needed.
plugins.overview:
Use this bb from your phone, tablet or another laptop on the same home network, in the device's browser. No bb account, no getbb.app and nothing to install on the device.

## What you get

- A "LAN access" switch. When it is on, bb answers on port 38890 on your local network, at its LAN IP address (such as `http://192.168.1.20:38890`), at any name you add yourself, and at the computer's Bonjour name (such as `http://macbook-pro.local:38890`).
- A settings section, on the plugin's page and on bb's Mobile settings page, that shows the URLs, pairs new devices with a QR code and lists paired devices with a Revoke button.
- `bb lan status`, `on`, `off`, `pair`, `devices` and `revoke` in the terminal, so agents and scripts can do the same.
- The full bb app on the device: threads stream live, and terminals work.

## Pairing

Press "Pair a device" or run `bb lan pair`. You get a QR code, a link and an eight-character code. The link uses your first extra hostname, or the LAN IP address when you have none, because many phones cannot resolve `.local` names. Scan the code or open the link on the device and press "Pair this device". The code works once and expires after five minutes. The device then stays paired for 400 days, or until you revoke it. Revoking a device closes its open connection at once. A device pairs once for each name it uses, so use one name per device.

## Names you can use

- The LAN IP addresses, listed in the status. Give the computer a fixed address in your router (a DHCP reservation): a device pairs per address, so a new address means pairing again.
- The computer's `.local` name, which Macs and most Linux machines announce on the network by themselves. Macs and iPhones resolve it; many Android phones and some Wi-Fi networks do not.
- Your own name, such as `bb.home.arpa`: add a DNS record for it in your router or Pi-hole that points at this computer, then add it under "Extra hostnames".
- On macOS you can set the port to 80 to drop the port from the URL.

## Security

- Only devices with private-network addresses are answered, and only for the names above. Tailscale addresses are refused.
- Devices that have not paired never reach bb. They see the pairing page.
- A paired device can do everything you can do in bb, including running commands in terminals. Pair only your own devices, and revoke one you lose.
- Requests that another website starts in a paired browser are refused, except plain links that open the app.
- Without HTTPS, traffic and the device cookie travel unencrypted, and browsers block voice input and clipboard access. To serve HTTPS, make a certificate (for example with mkcert, and install its root certificate on each device) and set the certificate and key file settings.

## Not included

- The native bb mobile app pairs only through getbb.app, so it cannot use LAN Connect. Use the phone's browser.
- Sharing agents' dev-server ports, and publishing extra `.local` names.

plugins.description: Run a software project with agents: a planner turns a goal into a validated spec and tickets, workers pick up tickets in their own worktrees, separate reviewers approve or request changes, and approved work merges into an integration branch or opens a pull request.
plugins.overview:
Run a software project with agents: a planner turns a goal into a validated spec and a ticket board, workers build the tickets in their own git worktrees, separate reviewers approve or ask for changes, and approved work merges into an integration branch or opens as pull requests. You watch and steer it from a full-screen page in bb's left navigation, or from `bb loom`.

## What you get

- A planner skill (`loom-plan`): any thread can propose a project as a TOML spec with tickets, acceptance criteria, checks, a review policy and a merge strategy. The plugin validates it with numbered errors you can act on, and you approve it before anything runs.
- Start a project from the page: New project opens bb's own new-thread composer, and the planner's questions, its draft and the Approve and Start buttons stay on the page.
- Review a spec without reading TOML: a dashboard with the tickets in dependency waves, shared files, the checks and the limits. Press "+ note" on any part to send the planner your notes in one message, and compare its versions with what each one changed.
- Workers that start by themselves: one thread per ready ticket, in its own worktree, only when its dependencies are done and its files do not overlap work in flight. The plugin, not the agent, commits, runs your check commands, and decides whether the work passed.
- Reviewers on their own model: each ticket is read by fresh reviewer threads that approve or send findings back to the worker. A ticket merges only after the review you asked for and the `after_merge` checks on the merged result.
- A Loom page: a home table that puts what needs you in each project's row, a health strip per project, a board with a lane per ticket state, an Agents tab with every thread, a live feed, and flow and agent metrics over 7, 14 or 30 days.
- A timeline on every project: rewind the whole page to any moment, or play it back, to see the board, agents and metrics as they were.
- Controls with a second click: a next-step bar on every project says what happens next and carries the one button you need now; start, pause, resume, land and archive a project; requeue, block or cancel a ticket; reply to a worker. Each is logged as your action. Approving the planner's fixed spec requeues the tickets whose worker or reviewer bb could not start.
- A header chip such as `CSV-3 · review` on worker, reviewer and planner threads that opens the ticket on the page, and a Planning chip on a planning conversation that opens it there.
- Questions the planner asks with Ask User Question appear above its chat on the page, where you answer them, and the Loom icon in the navigation rail counts what needs you.
- A ticket page that reads at a glance: its stage and a summary, each attempt as a card with its checks, review findings and merge, and its brief.
- `bb loom metrics`, `feed` and `report` print the numbers, the events and a finished project's record. A done hook in Loom's settings sends that record, or an agent's summary of it, to a command you choose.

## How it works

Every change to a project or ticket goes through one store method that appends an event in the same transaction, and the event table refuses edits. The metrics are computed from that log, so they are exact and can be recomputed. Agents get narrow tools for their role and never merge or push. On the integration strategy the branch stays local until you run `bb loom land`: one pull request upstream, or with `--direct` a push to the base branch. A blocked ticket reaches the planner in a triage round, and so does your reply on it.

## Requirements

- `git` on the machine that has the project's checkout.
- `gh`, signed in, for the pull request strategy and for `bb loom land`, and a GitHub remote.
- Provider usage: every worker, reviewer and planner is an ordinary bb thread, so your providers' usage and limits apply to all of them. Set a token budget or a deadline in the spec to have the plugin pause the project for you.

plugins.description: Let your own pi setup write bb's thread titles and commit messages: your credentials and model, no bb account needed. Adds a one-click regenerate-title button to the thread header and its actions menu, plus pi executable and model knobs in the plugin settings.
plugins.overview:
Delegate bb's helper AI tasks to the pi CLI on your machine.

## What you get

- bb's thread titles and commit messages generated by your own pi setup: your credentials, your model, your defaults — no bb account or separate API key needed.
- A Model knob and a Pi executable knob under Settings → Installed plugins → Pi AI Services (also editable with `bb plugin config pi-services`).
- A refresh button in the thread header that regenerates the current thread's title on demand, and the same action as **Regenerate title with pi** in every thread's actions menu. Phones get only the menu item, to keep their header uncluttered.

## How it works

The plugin registers a bb AI service that runs `pi --print --no-session --no-tools` on the machine that runs the bb server, optionally passing `--model` from the settings. bb calls it for thread titles and commit messages and cleans up the reply itself. The regenerate button and menu item call the plugin's own RPC, which asks pi for a fresh title and renames the thread.

Select the service under Settings → AI services, or run:

```sh
bb settings ai-services set thread-title pi
bb settings ai-services set commit-message pi
```

Automatic picks Pi CLI when bb cloud is not signed in.

## Limits

Text only: voice transcription is not provided. The pi CLI must be installed and signed in on the machine that runs the bb server; the plugin launches it as a one-shot process, so every call pays pi's startup cost. pi's tools are disabled (`--no-tools`) because bb asks for plain-text replies, and bb aborts text services after five seconds.

plugins.description: Gives a thread a title when bb's automatic title fails or times out, using the same Shopify AI model. `bb retitle <thread>` titles any thread again, and `bb retitle --untitled` backfills threads bb left untitled.
plugins.overview:
Titles the threads that bb's automatic titling leaves untitled.

bb asks its AI service for a title once, when a thread starts, and gives up if the answer takes more than 8 seconds. The thread then keeps the first 80 characters of your message as its name. Retitle notices and titles it with the Shopify AI proxy.

## What you get

- Automatic retry: about 10 seconds after a thread starts running, Retitle titles it if it is still untitled. Threads you renamed, hidden threads and prompts under five words (which bb leaves untitled on purpose) are left alone.
- `bb retitle <thread>` titles one thread again, even one that already has a title. Run inside a thread, `bb retitle` titles that thread.
- `bb retitle --untitled` backfills the newest 20 untitled, unarchived threads. Add `--limit <n>`, `--project <id>`, `--dry-run` to list them first, or `--json`.

## Better titles for command prompts

bb titles from everything in the first message, including the instructions a `!command` mention attaches out of your sight, such as the whole body of `~/.agents/commands/plan.md`. Retitle reads only what you typed and tells the model which commands you invoked, so a `!plan` thread is titled after the work, not the planner instructions.

## How it works

Retitle uses bb's own title prompt and the title model chosen in the Shopify AI plugin's settings (`bb plugin config shopify-ai`), and falls back to GLM 5.3 Flash when that plugin is missing or its model is not a chat-completions model. The proxy token comes from `SHOPIFY_PROXY_KEY` or `devx llm-gateway print-token --key` on the machine that runs the bb server.

## Limits

- Shopify only: it needs access to the Shopify AI proxy.
- Threads that start while the plugin is not loaded are not retried; run `bb retitle --untitled` to catch them.
- The automatic retry runs once per thread per bb server run.

plugins.description: Check what an agent actually ran, changed and decided, in one live log beside the chat. Messages, thinking, commands with their output and exit codes, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps appear in timeline order, with a timestamp on every row and a duration on every command. It also shows what bb gives the agent but keeps out of the chat, such as plugin steers and mention context, marked Hidden. The log follows new output as it arrives, opens failed commands by default, and filters to messages, thinking, tools, hidden input or errors. Search covers the whole session and highlights every match, and single keys jump between rows, replies, errors and matches. Open it with Mod+Shift+L or from the thread header; it reads bb's timeline and keeps no copy of the thread.
plugins.overview:
See everything an agent did in a thread without opening nested chat rows.

## What you get

- One flat side-panel log in bb's timeline order: your messages and steers, child reports, agent replies, thinking, commands, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps.
- What bb gives the agent but keeps out of the chat, marked Hidden where the agent received it: a plugin's steer, the context a mention resolves to, an automatic retry or a suppressed tool result.
- Rows tinted by type in your bb theme's colors, so replies, tool calls, commands, file changes and failures stand apart.
- Timestamps, status, exit codes and duration beside each step. Replies appear in full, long output previews its first and last lines, failed commands and tools open by default, and `x` expands every row.
- Filters for Messages, Thinking, Tools, Hidden and Errors, plus whole-session search that paints every match in amber and the current one in orange, with a counter and next/previous arrows (Enter and Shift+Enter in the search box). The log follows new output, including outputs that open up as they finish, until you scroll up or move to an older row; “↓ Latest” or `G` takes you back.
- Keyboard navigation (`j/k`, `n/N` for replies, or for matches while searching, `e/E` for errors), copy (`c`), a message link back to chat (`s`), and Mod+Shift+L to open the tab. The thread header has an open button too, except on phones, where the right panel's tab list opens the log. bb's Maximize pane button gives the log the whole window.
- Settings for preview sizes, whether failures open by themselves, which rows show when the log opens (hidden messages included), a 12- or 24-hour clock, and whether rows are tinted by type. Changes reach open panels straight away.

## How it works

The plugin loads bb's public timeline API, including nested rows, when you open the tab. It applies live deltas afterward, with at most two refresh requests a second. Because the timeline leaves hidden input out, it also reads the thread's request events and places each hidden message by its sequence number. It does not change bb's chat markup or store thread data; only the expanded-view choice is saved on this device. If you also want bb's chat itself to stop folding finished turns, use `bb settings completed-turns <provider> flat`.

## Limits

bb truncates output above 32,000 characters and the log keeps its truncation note. A match inside an expanded file diff is not painted, because bb's diff viewer keeps its own styles; stepping still frames its row. The whole session is fetched on opening, including large threads.

plugins.description: See which agent threads failed, need you or are still running, grouped under your bb sections. Child threads nest under their parent across projects, and a collapsed parent still shows its most urgent child. A status-lanes view lists every awake thread under Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle. Drag threads to reorder, nest or move them between sections, and snooze a quiet family until tomorrow morning. Hover a row for the thread's model, context use, branch, uncommitted changes and pull request. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each bb client.
plugins.overview:
Keep parallel agent threads readable and make triage part of the sidebar.

## What you get

- Your bb sections as coloured groups, with Pinned first and unfiled Threads last. Children form a tree across projects and sections; their own state and a collapsed parent's urgent descendants remain visible at a glance.
- A title, project, section and branch filter, status chips, three densities and an in-list View options menu, with short hints on the controls. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each bb client.
- An Archive toggle shows archived threads on a shelf at the end of the list, with Unarchive and older pages on demand.
- A status-lanes view groups every awake thread under its own Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle state, newest attention first. An optional Needs-you shelf repeats urgent threads at the top without duplicating bb shortcuts.
- Hover a thread for an info card: model, context use, branch, changes, pull request and, in the Briefing layout, its first prompt and latest reply.

## Organize and triage

Drag threads above, below or under another thread, or onto a section header. Alt+arrow keys move a focused thread; Alt-click and Shift-click select families for bulk moves, archive and snooze. Section menus rename, colour, sort and add threads, and can set a default project that the section's + button uses for new threads. New sections start as an empty name field in place, and nothing is created until you press Enter. By-hand, recent-activity and status sort modes apply per section or to Threads. Sorted roots cannot be manually reordered, but you can still nest threads or move them onto a sorted section's header.

Idle unpinned families fade after your chosen number of days (three by default). A section menu can archive only its stale roots after a confirmation that counts their children, with Undo. Snooze a quiet family until 09:00 tomorrow (or your chosen local hour); the Snoozed shelf shows when it wakes and has a Wake button. New attention or an urgent or running child wakes it early.

Palette commands focus the filter (Mod+Alt+F), jump to the next failed or waiting thread (Mod+Alt+J), switch views and create a section.

## Parent threads and limits

Making a thread a child tells its parent's agent; bb then sends the parent each finished child turn. Undo within two seconds sends nothing, and bb allows at most four levels. Switchboard leaves parents, sections, pins and archives in bb, while its plugin store holds order, colour, collapse, sort, default projects and snooze. Status lanes reorder by design; the list does not window rows.

plugins.description: See every worktree your parallel agents work in, and everything they changed across repositories, from the parent thread. Each worktree shows status, branch, commits ahead and behind, uncommitted files and its pull request; open one to read its diffs and commits, talk to its agent, or start a terminal in it. Files changed in two worktrees are flagged before they conflict. A full-screen Vantage page in bb's left navigation shows every recent thread's worktrees and changed repositories at once, filtered by project. It paints at once and loads git details in the background; archived threads stay hidden on the page until you ask for them.
plugins.overview:
See how every agent's worktree is doing, open any one of them to read its diffs, commits and conversation, and see everything your threads changed across repositories: for one thread's tree in its side panel, or for every recent thread on a full-screen page.

## What you get

- A Vantage tab in a thread's side panel, with a thread header button (not on phones) and a palette command. It opens on the Worktrees view.
- One row for each worktree in the thread tree: the parent's own checkout, every child's worktree, and the kept branch of every archived child. A row shows bb's status glyph (running, needs you, failed, finished), the branch, commits ahead and behind, uncommitted files, line counts and the pull request.
- A row for a checkout a thread made outside bb, such as a clone made from a shell, once the thread both edited a file in it and ran commands in it, with every change in it, even ones made by shell commands.
- A thread working on its base branch, such as `main`, reads "on base" and lists the commits it made there.
- Works with any environment provider, including ones that place a thread in a repository's subfolder or keep its folder after archiving.
- A warning when files are changed in more than one worktree of a project, so you see a possible conflict before you merge.
- Click a row to open that worktree. Changes shows uncommitted and committed files with diffs, Commits shows each commit and its files, and Chat shows the child's conversation, where you can approve a request or steer the agent.
- Terminal here opens a shell in the worktree's folder. Open thread opens the child; bb's thread menu offers stop, archive and more. The keys [ and ] step between worktrees and Escape goes back.
- The Repositories view groups everything the thread tree changed by repository: thread workspaces, other checkouts agents edited by path, archived children's branches, and recorded edits for files outside any repository.
- A full-screen Vantage page in bb's left navigation covers every thread active in the last 24 hours, plus anything running and threads archived in that time. The worktree list, grouped by project, sits on the left; the selected worktree's changes, commits, chat and terminal on the right. Filter by project, by text, or to worktrees with changes only. Each view has an address, so back and forward work. "Open full screen" in a thread's tab opens the page for just that thread's tree.
- Both views paint every row at once and fill in the git numbers as they arrive. The page starts without archived threads; ticking "Include archived" adds them below the active ones without touching the active rows, and the side tab includes them by default.

## For agents

`bb vantage worktrees` prints one line for each worktree, then the shared files. `bb vantage worktree <thread>` prints one thread's files and commits. `bb vantage changes` prints the Repositories view. Each accepts `--json`; `--thread <id>` reads another thread, and `--all` (with `--hours <n>`) reads every recent thread, grouped by project, and `--archived` adds the archived ones.

## How it works

Vantage only reads. It never stages, commits or changes a file. A workspace's counts come from one bb status call that both views share, and its status and pull request from data bb's sidebar already loads. Other checkouts are read with git on the machine that owns them. Results are kept for 60 seconds and reloaded where an agent's edit or a workspace change touched; git roots for 10 minutes. Two settings tune it: the time window (24 hours) and the thread limit (200).

## Limits

- 500 files per list, 100 commits per worktree, patches cut at 1 MiB.
- Terminal here needs a worktree on disk, in the side panel on the thread's machine.
- A checkout outside bb gets its own row only after the thread has both edited a file in it and changed into it with `cd`, `pushd` or `git -C` and an absolute or `~/` path. Shell-only work in a repository the thread never edited is still missed.
